title: Dominic and the Bell
premise: Vesper Nakamura arrives at St. Aldhelm's Academy to teach, but students keep vanishing from attendance rolls while the school insists they never existed. When an excavation crew behind the gym unearths a door sealed from the inside, Vesper's meticulous records become the only map of who was taken and when. The door opens onto a buried wing where the missing live on in a looping school day, sustained by a bell that counts them — and the count must reach a number before anyone can leave. To get the family out ahead of the final toll, Vesper must sacrifice the documented truth of their own identity, because the bell only releases what it cannot remember.
about_author: Edmund Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the records of defunct boarding schools before turning to fiction. He writes at night, he says, because paper tells the truth more honestly in the dark.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Vesper Nakamura's POV. Arriving at St. Aldhelm's, Vesper begins the ritual of documenting everything: classrooms, colleagues, the strange hush after last bell. A student named Idris is marked absent, then erased from the register entirely by morning. The beat is quiet unease — the comfort of record-keeping curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Third-period English has four empty desks no one acknowledges. Headmaster Corvane explains, smoothly, that enrollment fluctuates. Vesper cross-references old yearbooks and finds faces that appear in photos but in no files. Emotional beat: the first crack in institutional trust, and Vesper's growing sense that documentation is a form of prayer to something listening.

chapters.title: Idris's Locker
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with a brief shift to custodian Marta Hale. Inside Idris's locker: a child's drawing of a door with a handle on the inside. Marta admits she's swept up small shoes for years and said nothing, for her pension's sake. Beat: complicity and guilt; loyalty to the school beginning to war with loyalty to the truth.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Danny Okafor's POV. Groundbreaking for the new annex unearths a stone lintel stamped with the school's founding date — fifty years before the school existed. Corvane orders it covered by nightfall. Danny photographs everything anyway. Beat: working-class pragmatism colliding with institutional power; the reader sees Corvane's fear for the first time.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Danny and Vesper's alternating POV. The crew breaks through to a bronze door whose bolts are thrown from within. Scratched beside it: tally marks, thousands deep. That night the school bell rings though it was disconnected decades ago. Beat: dread made physical; Vesper realizes the count has already started.

chapters.title: What the Register Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Comparing a century of registers, Vesper finds the vanishings follow a pattern — every 25 years, always in autumn, always ending when the count reaches one hundred names. The current tally stands at ninety-six. Beat: cold clarity; the horror becomes arithmetic, and arithmetic can be raced.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Vesper's framing POV. The four most recent missing are identified: Idris, two students, and a teacher who 'resigned' in September. Vesper recruits Danny and Marta. Corvane catches them in the archive and, instead of punishing them, begs them to stop — his own brother is inside. Beat: the antagonist revealed as another hostage of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. At dawn the bolts withdraw on their own. Cold air smelling of chalk dust pours out. Danny's camera shows the corridor beyond as it was in 1974. Marta steps back; Vesper steps forward. Beat: threshold terror and the pull of the unknown — the door wants witnesses.

chapters.title: The Buried Wing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Beyond the door: a perfect replica of the school's east wing, lit by windows showing an overcast day that never changes. Desks hold half-finished lessons. And there is Idris, older than his absence, who greets Vesper like a substitute teacher expected for years. Beat: uncanny warmth — the horror here is hospitality.

chapters.title: The Bell Counts
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He explains the rules gently: the bell tolls each time someone new remembers them fully. Ninety-nine remembered souls and the hundredth toll ends the loop — everyone stays forever, perfectly preserved. Forgetting is the only exit, and forgetting hurts like drowning. Beat: tragic inversion; memory, Vesper's religion, is the enemy.

chapters.title: Miss Adeyemi's Classroom
chapters.summary: POV of Grace Adeyemi, the vanished teacher. She has taught the same lesson for three months and knows it, and teaches it anyway, because routine keeps the others calm. She recognizes Vesper's name from a staff memo she'll never answer. Beat: dignity under erasure; Grace chooses the children's peace over her own rescue.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV, present day. He reveals the school's founders built the wing deliberately: a machine to keep beloved dead 'safe' by feeding the bell their memories. His brother went in voluntarily in 1999. Every headmaster since has guarded the secret. Beat: power's corruption shown as inheritance — evil maintained by people who love someone.

chapters.title: Marta's Debt
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Thirty years ago Marta found the door as a young cleaner and was paid to forget. Now she remembers everything at once and the bell tolls — ninety-seven. Guilt becomes action: she gives Vesper the founder's ledger she stole and hid. Beat: redemption purchased with danger; the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Ninety-Eight
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. A curious student, Priya, follows the adults, slips through the door, and sees her missing brother. Her joy is total recall. The bell tolls ninety-eight and the wing's false daylight dims a shade. Beat: grief and fury — love itself is the mechanism of the trap.

chapters.title: The Founder's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The ledger reveals the design flaw: the bell holds what it remembers, so it must be made to forget. The countermeasure requires someone to stand in the belfry and feed it a complete life — every memory, every name — until it chokes. Beat: terrible hope; Vesper understands the price and starts lying to the group about who will pay it.

chapters.title: Grace's Bargain
chapters.summary: Grace's POV. Grace offers herself: she has already begun forgetting her own surname, so she has less to lose. Vesper refuses — and realizes refusing means volunteering. They argue in the empty corridor while the trapped children sleep in their looping dormitory. Beat: moral climax approaching; loyalty vs. truth made intimate.

chapters.title: Priya Runs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Panicking, Priya tries to drag her brother out bodily. The wing resists — corridors lengthen, doors multiply. Danny hauls both children back as the bell tolls ninety-nine, early, hungry. One name remains. Beat: peak external tension; the family must move tonight or not at all.

chapters.title: The Belfry
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Above the buried wing hangs the original bell, rope worn smooth by generations. Vesper ties themselves to the rope and begins reciting their own archive aloud — every entry, every name, every page of the prayer they've written all book long. Beat: sacrificial resolve; documentation becomes literal self-immolation.

chapters.title: One Hundred
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs — Grace, Danny, Idris — as the bell tolls the hundredth time and the wing convulses. Vesper's voice frays into static; their face goes unplaceable even to the reader. The trapped begin to surface toward the door, forgetting as they climb. Beat: climax; triumph and loss indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Headcount
chapters.summary: Danny's POV, aftermath. Forty-one people emerge into the excavation pit at dawn, blinking, holding hands with siblings they can't name. Corvane collapses weeping over a brother who walks past him without recognition. The bell hangs silent, cracked. Beat: exhausted relief shadowed by cost — rescue achieved, memory forfeited.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Page
chapters.summary: Grace's POV. Rebuilding her life above ground, Grace keeps a notebook of things people tell her about herself, since she cannot remember. Vesper visits — polite, kind, a stranger — and leaves a gift: the full archive, printed, so that others may remember what Vesper gave away. Beat: bittersweet grace; identity survives in other people's keeping.

chapters.title: Last Bell
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, fragmented and serene. Vesper remains as the school's quiet caretaker of the sealed door, unable to say why the work feels like devotion. On the final page of the archive, in handwriting almost their own: 'If you are reading this, you knew me. Please write it down.' Beat: haunting resolution — the prayer continues, addressed now to us.
